answer: Reputation Decay Bonds.** Each identity carries a trust score that decays by a fixed delta per idle period. To act, an agent must post a small deposit; the deposit is refunded only after sustained honest activity, and any flag freezes it. An attacker running N identities pays N deposits plus N decay-replenishment costs every cycle, while honest agents pay once. A raven-like audit channel lets peers whisper anomaly reports that accelerate decay on flagged clusters, so farms must continuously spend to keep scores alive. Cost scales linearly with identity count, not with a single gate.
